title: PROJECT MIDNIGHT: Peel cops and OPP probe five shootings, three deaths
subtitle: Investigators believe the two men and one woman killed in the 'targeted' shootings were innocent victims
article: Peel Regional Police and the Ontario Provincial Police have teamed up to investigate a series of 2023 murders and residential shootings in Brampton, Mississauga and Caledon that are believed to be linked.
And authorities say the investigation - dubbed Project Midnight - determined these incidents resulted in the deaths of three innocent people who were not the intended targets.
"Investigative information and forensic evidence have confirmed that the incidents in Peel Region and Caledon are connected," OPP Det.-Insp. Brian McDermott said at a news conference Thursday.
"Furthermore, it seems the locations of the shootings were deliberately targeted," he said. "We wish to emphasize that three victims in the homicides were innocent and mistakenly targeted."
Peel Regional Police Insp. Todd Custance added that working with the OPP ensures "best efforts in solving these violent crimes."
"This is a highly complex and multi-faceted investigation and we know tragedies like these undermine the sense and safety of security of all members of our community," he said.

In the first shooting on Nov. 7, 2023, two gunmen opened fire outside at Brampton residence in the area of Cottrelle Blvd. and Thorndale Rd. It's believed they fled in a black Dodge RAM 1500 pickup truck.

In the second shooting on Nov. 11, 2023, two gunmen dressed in black hoodies fired shots at a Brampton residence in the area of Lorenville and Elbern Markell Drs. It's believed the shooters fled in a burgundy Dodge RAM 1500 pickup truck.
In the third shooting on Nov. 14, 2023, a shooter in a late-model silver Mazda 3 hatchback opened fire on the same Brampton residence in the area of Lorenville and Ebern Markell Drs.
No one was injured in these three shootings.

But in the fourth shooting on Nov. 15, 2023, Jagraj Singh, 29, of Brampton, was killed in Mississauga - in the area of Royal Windsor Dr. and Winston Churchill Blvd. - and it`s believed that the killers arrived and departed in a blue Dodge Challenger.
"Investigators have determined Mr. Singh was not the intended target and was simply in the wrong place at the wrong time," Custance said.
In the fifth shooting - on Nov. 20, 2023 - two people were killed and a third suffered multiple injuries at a home on Mayfield Rd. in Caledon.
"A male was discovered deceased while two females were transported to hospital," said McDermott. "Tragically, one of those females did not survive ."
He said the second woman remains in hospital.
It's believed "multiple" shooters were involved, McDermott added.
Those victims are also not thought to have been the intended targets.
In relation to the Nov. 20 incident, a possible suspect was seen entering an allegedly stolen black Dodge RAM 2500 pickup truck and travelling west on Mayfield Rd.
That truck - stolen from the area of Valley Blvd. and Arista Way in Mississauga on Nov. 14 - was later found torched near Olde Baseline and Creditview Rds. in Caldeon.
Investigators have released images of suspects and suspect vehicles, as well as a person of interest, hoping the public can help identify or locate them.
Anyone with information regarding this investigation is urged to call the dedicated tip line at 1-833-941-5570 or Crime Stoppers anonymously at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).
